methodology: Token counts are not persisted in run artifacts (run_meta.json stores only task_id, run_id, seed, condition; no LLM usage data is saved). Estimates are derived from elapsed_sec across 3,096 runs (oracle n=563, restricted n=575, team_no_plan n=605, team_no_verify n=652, full n=701) using a conservative throughput assumption of 150 tokens/sec for Gemini 3 Flash (the reference model). This figure is consistent with Gemini Flash API latency benchmarks at typical task-length outputs. Elapsed time includes tool execution overhead, so true LLM token throughput is higher; estimates are therefore conservative lower bounds.

notes.oracle_single_agent: Oracle is a single agent with full spec access; ~129s avg => ~19K tokens/run covering system prompt, task spec, up to 30 turns of tool use.
notes.team_full_three_agents: Full team (planner + executor + verifier) runs 3 sequential agents; ~610s avg => ~91K tokens/run, reflecting 3x agent overhead plus inter-agent message context accumulation.
notes.cost_ratio_interpretation: Team runs consume ~4.7x more tokens than oracle runs on average, consistent with 3 agents each running ~half the turns of a solo oracle agent.
notes.caveat: Estimates assume no tool-execution dead time dominates; for tasks with heavy bash execution (e.g. DIST, CRYPTO), elapsed_sec overestimates LLM time and true token counts may be 30-50% lower.
